newsitem.title: UK: Lack of transparency blurs gold's role in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Lack of transparency blurs gold's role in Europe.

text.p: Gold's role in European central bank reserves and the attitude of the financial institutions to the metal are still unclear despite debate, a mining official told the 5th Central Bank Conference on Tuesday.
Tom Main, chief executive of the South African Chamber of Mines, said gold lacked transparency as was witnessed by the Internationl Monetary Fund (IMF) and its debate on selling gold.
Main said there was also no differentiation between gold and foreign exchange in European central bank reserves which also continued the uncertainty.
Regarding the IMF, he said: "We need to acknowledge that sales are more likely to take place than not. But the question is how much."

The talk had been of five million ounces but at the same time there had been debate on funding the restructuring programme to remove debt from the world's poorest countries through "bilaterals" as well, he said.

The possibility of a sale had caused psychological damage in gold producing countries. "It might have been better for the IMF to have financed the seeking and development of gold reserves in some of the poorer countries," he said.
Even with the many changes in the gold market over the past 10 years there were still regulatory barriers.
In some parts of Europe, gold still could not be held as an investment asset and there were also guidelines which hindered investment in gold.
"There is an enormous process still to take place," he said.
